title: A morning at Eminönü
goal: Follow a story of street life told with compound verbs, and tell one of your own.

intro.text: This lesson mixes the whole unit in a morning at Eminönü, Istanbul's old harbour: a simit seller, a hungry seagull and an old man with a story. Look out for the second verb in each compound: *ver-*, *kal-*, *dur-*, *yaz-*, *gel-*.

vocab.en: pier, landing stage (vapur iskelesi: ferry pier)
to treat (someone to something); to order
child, son or daughter (evladım: my child, said to a young person)

exercises.title: Eminönü'nde bir sabah
exercises.passage:
Cumartesi sabahı Eminönü'ne indim. Vapur iskelesinin önünde bir simitçi, başındaki tepsiyle bağırıp duruyordu: “Taze simit, sıcak simit!” Bir simit alıp denize doğru yürüdüm. Martılar başımızın üstünde dönüp duruyordu.

İlk ısırığı alacaktım, ama bir martı elimdeki simidi kapıverdi. Ne olduğunu anlamadan bakakaldım. Şaşkınlıktan az kalsın iskeleden denize düşüyordum. Yanımdaki yaşlı bir adam gülmeye başladı: “Burada martılar simidi senden önce yer, evladım.” Sonra simitçiye döndü: “Bu gence bir simit daha ver, benden olsun.”

Simitçi yeni simidi bana uzatıverdi. “Siz yiyedurun, ben martılara bakarım.” dedi. Adamla birlikte iskelede oturup çay içtik. Bana kırk yıldır her sabah buraya gelip vapurları izlediğini anlattı. “Şehir çok değişti, ama simitle çay hiç değişmedi.” dedi.
exercises.translation: On Saturday morning I went down to Eminönü. In front of the ferry pier a simit seller, with his tray on his head, kept shouting: “Fresh simit, hot simit!” I bought a simit and walked towards the sea. Seagulls kept circling above our heads. I was about to take the first bite, but a seagull snatched the simit out of my hand. Before I knew what was happening, I just stood there staring. I was so surprised I nearly fell off the pier into the sea. An old man next to me started laughing: “Here the seagulls eat your simit before you do, son.” Then he turned to the simit seller: “Give this young man another simit, it's on me.” The simit seller handed me the new simit. “You go ahead and eat, I'll keep an eye on the seagulls,” he said. The old man and I sat on the pier and drank tea. He told me that for forty years he had come here every morning to watch the ferries. “The city has changed a lot, but simit and tea haven't changed at all,” he said.

questions.q: What happened to the narrator's first simit?
options: He dropped it in the sea
He gave it to the old man
questions.explain: *Bir martı elimdeki simidi kapıverdi*: `-(y)Iver` for something sudden.

questions.q: Who paid for the second simit?
options: No one: the seller gave it for free
questions.explain: *Bu gence bir simit daha ver, benden olsun*: **it's on me**.

questions.q: What does *bakakaldım* tell us about the narrator?
options: He was too surprised to react
He kept looking around for the seagull
He looked at the sea for a long time
questions.explain: `-(y)Akal`: frozen in a state, here from surprise.

exercises.question: In the story, *Şaşkınlıktan az kalsın iskeleden denize düşüyordum.* Which compound verb says the same thing?

why.3: `-(y)Adur` is **carry on**, used in commands and suggestions.

exercises.text: Martılar dönüp ___, biri simidimi kap___ ve ben bak___.
exercises.en: The seagulls kept circling, one of them snatched my simit, and I just stood there staring.

accept: ıverdi

reject.why: The last vowel of *kap-* is a, so the linking vowel is ı: *kapıverdi*.

accept: akaldım

reject.why: *Bakıp kaldım* is also heard, but this blank wants the one-word compound: *bakakaldım*.

exercises.explain: *dön-üp dur-uyor-du* (kept circling), *kap-ıver-di* (snatched, suddenly), *bak-akal-dı-m* (I stood there staring).

exercises.prompt: Could you just squeeze some lemon on top?
accept: Üstüne biraz limon sıkıverir misiniz?
Üstüne biraz limon sıkıverir misin?
Sen üstüne biraz limon sıkıverir misin?
Siz üstüne biraz limon sıkıverir misiniz?
Üzerine biraz limon sıkıverir [misin|misiniz]?

reject.answer: Üstüne biraz limon sıkıp verir misiniz?
reject.why: `-(y)Iver` is one word with the stem: *sıkıverir*.

exercises.hint: *sıkmak* is **to squeeze**; the top of it is *üstü*, with the dative.
exercises.explain: *sık-ıver-ir misiniz?*: a small favour asked of the seller, with *siz*.

exercises.en: The simit seller has been shouting since this morning.

exercises.prompt: You go ahead and eat, I'll keep an eye on the seagulls.
accept: Siz yiyedurun, martılara ben bakarım.
Yiyedurun, ben martılara bakarım.

exercises.prompt: Let me treat you to a simit.
accept: Sana bir simit ısmarlayayım.
size bir simit ısmarlayayım.
Ben sana bir simit ısmarlayayım.
Ben size bir simit ısmarlayayım.
(Ben) [sana|size] bir simit ısmarlayıvereyim.

reject.why: The verb *ısmarlamak* takes the person treated in the dative: *sana*.

exercises.explain: To treat, *ısmarlamak*: the person in the dative, the treat as the object. **Let me** is the optative *-ayım*.

context.tr: Midyeci yine aynı şarkıyı söyleyip duruyor.
context.en: The mussel seller keeps singing the same song again.
Don't look at him, carry on eating your mussels.

exercises.question: How does Ece feel about the mussel seller's singing?
options: She finds it a bit annoying.
She wants him to sing another song.
She is surprised he can sing.

why.1: Nothing in her words asks for another song.

exercises.explain: `-(y)Ip durmak` with *yine*: it keeps happening, and she is tired of it. Can answers with a kind `-(y)Adur`: *yiyedur*.

reject.answer: Hırsız çantayı kapıp durdu, ama polis onu yakaladı.
reject.why: *Kapıp durdu* would mean he kept grabbing it. **Grabbed and ran off** is *kapıp kaçtı*.

exercises.explain: *Kapıp kaçmak* (to snatch and run) works as one verb; *yakalamak* is **to catch**.

exercises.task: Tell a small surprising moment on a street, a market or a ferry in three or four sentences. Use at least two compound verbs from this unit, for example `-(y)Iver`, `-(y)Akal` and `-(y)Ip durmak`.
models: Geçen hafta Kadıköy'de bir kestaneciden kestane aldım. Paramı uzatırken bir çocuk koşup gelip elimdeki kestaneyi kapıverdi. Ben bakakaldım, kestaneci ise gülüp durdu. Sonunda bana bir kestane daha verdi.
Dün vapurda bir martı masamıza konuverdi. Herkes donakaldı. Martı bir süre etrafa bakıp durdu, sonra bir simit kapıp uçtu.
checklist: At least two compound verbs: *kapıverdi*, *bakakaldım*, *gülüp durdu*, *donakaldı*…
The past *-DI* for the events of the story, with the person on the second verb: *bakakaldım*
`-(y)Iver` written as one word, `-(y)Ip durmak` as two
Places with the locative (*vapurda*) and the people involved in the right case (*kestaneciden*)
